findings.title: agent() label/phase are never persisted; workflow node names exist only as an orchestrator prompt convention
The rich workflow_agent graph record (label/phase/state/tokens/attempt) is in-memory only and flushed to <sessionId>/workflows/<runId>.json exactly once, at run completion
Journal entries carry no timestamps and journal append order is not spawn order (proved against 6 parallel agents)
One logical node emits many 'started' entries with new agentIds (180s stall watchdog, up to 5 retries); the stale-close guard never closes the abandoned ones
Journal key is a content hash of prompt+{schema,model,effort,isolation,agentType}: identical prompts collide and resumed runs replay agents with no journal entry
Queued-but-unstarted agents have zero on-disk footprint; concurrency cap is min(16,max(2,cpus-2)) so fan-outs shrink on small hosts
Transcript and run-snapshot paths key off the CURRENT session id, so /clear or /compact splits one run's data across sibling session dirs
toolUseResult.totalTokens is the last API call's usage, not a per-agent rollup (90,971 reported vs 1,235,241 actual)
No completion marker inside a subagent transcript; liveness needs three states because the harness's own stall threshold is 180s
spawnDepth does not encode workflow nesting (both kinds are depth 1) and workflow agents get no parentAgentId; the parent edge is only the directory name
Workflow-agent user-retry/user-skip leave no disk record; only Agent-tool sidecars get stoppedByUser, so terminated nodes are indistinguishable from crashed ones
Harness-derived vs convention-derived graph structure must be visually distinguished; queued nodes and loop edges are never harness facts
The session-to-workflow edge exists in exactly one parent-transcript toolUseResult (runId/transcriptDir/scriptPath); nothing else links them
Per-agent labels collide across parallel siblings: all six researchers emit label 'research #1'
Agent ids truncated to 8 chars in the event stream, breaking the join back to the 17-char transcript filename
Carried-over tasks' wf_dir paths are deleted, and the watcher's newest-journal fallback would attach the live run to a dead task
todos/ and <sessionId>/workflows/ are empty on this machine; sessions/<pid>.json is pid-keyed so stale entries survive a crashed CLI

result.summary: Rebuilt the run graph from primary sources (live session dd469822…, workflow wf_829e6f58-b2f, and grep/dd reads of the 2.1.220 CLI binary) and found 17 actionable items, 2 blockers. The harness writes, unconditionally: per-agent transcripts with timestamps and message.usage; sidecars carrying agentType/description/toolUseId/spawnDepth/model (and parentAgentId only for depth-2+); a workflow journal of bare {type,key,agentId[,result]} lines; and, in the parent transcript, the Agent tool_use/tool_result pair and the single Workflow tool_result that names runId/transcriptDir/scriptPath. Everything else a graph wants is either convention or unavailable. Two blockers: (1) the label/phase passed to agent() are never persisted, so every workflow node on disk is an anonymous "workflow-subagent · opus · spawnDepth 1" — node naming is entirely the [monitor] prompt-marker convention; (2) the rich node record (index/label/phaseTitle/state/tokens/toolCalls/durationMs/attempt/resultPreview) lives only in memory and is flushed to <sessionId>/workflows/<runId>.json at exactly one call site, in the completion path, so it cannot drive a live graph. Majors: journal lines have no timestamps and journal order is not spawn order (proved — append order differs from transcript-first-timestamp order for the 6 parallel researchers); a 180s stall watchdog with up to 5 retries makes one logical node emit multiple "started" entries with new agentIds, which decision_watcher's stale-close guard provably never closes (phantom forever-running nodes); the journal key is a content hash so identical prompts collide and resumed runs replay agents with no journal entry at all; queued agents have zero disk footprint and the concurrency cap is min(16,max(2,cpus-2)), so the same fan-out renders smaller on a small host; transcript and snapshot paths key off the CURRENT session id, so /clear or /compact scatters one run across sibling dirs; toolUseResult.totalTokens is only the LAST API call's usage (measured 90,971 vs 1,235,241 summed — a 14x under-report) while totalDurationMs/toolStats/resolvedModel are trustworthy; there is no completion marker inside a transcript (measured healthy flush gaps up to 30s against a 180s harness stall threshold), so liveness must be three-state; spawnDepth is 1 for both direct and workflow subagents so it does not encode nesting; and workflow-agent user-retry/user-skip write nothing to disk, so a Touch-issued termination is indistinguishable from a crash unless Touch keeps its own control audit. The file ends with a per-lifecycle-stage table of exactly what an n8n-style graph may honestly assert at each moment, and the recommendation to render harness-derived structure and convention/declared structure as visually distinct layers — since the README's pause/terminate controls would otherwise sit on nodes the harness never confirmed.

result.summary:
Stack/delivery research for Touch, verified empirically on this machine (probes in /tmp/claude-1000; nothing written to the live task folder except the two mandated status.sh calls and the findings file). 18 findings: 3 blockers, 9 major, 6 minor.

Two premises in the brief turned out to be false and change the design. (1) The firewall does NOT block package installs: `npm install @xterm/xterm dagre elkjs cytoscape mermaid` and a pip dry-run both succeeded through the CONNECT proxy. The real constraint is runtime offline-safety — the browser loading the page (especially from the host after `sbx ports --publish`) gets no proxy, so nothing may be fetched at page load. Rule to codify: stdlib-only at runtime, npm allowed only to vendor pinned, committed assets (note .gitignore:18-19 ignores node_modules/ and dist/, so vendored files must live at touch-visual/vendor/). (2) `node-pty` cannot build here — no g++ in the image (`make: g++: No such file or directory`), while Python's stdlib `pty` works end-to-end including TIOCSWINSZ resize, so the PTY tier must be Python.

Blockers. No local control channel exists on a running CLI: `messagingSocketPath` is emitted undefined in the 2.1.220 binary, no session sockets exist on disk, and `--remote-control` is an Anthropic cloud bridge (`/v1/sessions`, "will not appear in the Claude app"). Touch can only drive sessions it spawns itself; every other session is read-only transcript replay, and the sidebar must show the two classes differently. Spawning is booby-trapped: a `claude` launched from inside an agent session inherits `CLAUDE_CODE_CHILD_SESSION=1` and prints "Transcript saving is off" — verified live, and verified fixed by scrubbing CLAUDE*/AI_AGENT from the child env — which would silently starve the entire graph half of data. And the existing server binds 0.0.0.0 with no auth and never reads the Origin header: a probe handshake with `Origin: http://evil.example` got a 101, so adding keystroke input to that socket is cross-origin RCE against a session running --dangerously-skip-permissions with ~/.claude/.credentials.json readable.

Transport/terminal. The existing WS cannot receive: `parse_client_frames` deletes payloads without unmasking (monitor_server.py:307) and a masked client frame is silently dropped (verified). The 0.5s poll (monitor_server.py:378) is a latency floor no terminal survives; the verified alternative is `pty.openpty()` + `Popen(start_new_session=True)` + `loop.add_reader` inside asyncio (never `pty.fork()`). Captured bytes from a real claude TUI include alt-screen, mouse 1000/1002/1003/1006, bracketed paste, DA1 identification queries and 24-bit color, so xterm.js (489KB UMD + 7KB CSS) is required — hand-rolling means dropping the terminal-fidelity requirement. For the graph, do not vendor a layout engine (dagre.min 284KB, elk 1.6MB, cytoscape 435KB, mermaid 84MB installed): the loop DAG's ranks are fixed by the two workflow templates and monitor.html:296-318 already prototypes the flow strip — hand-roll layered SVG with stable node ids so updates patch rather than re-layout.

Control. Loop restart is an in-session `Workflow({scriptPath, resumeFromRunId})` tool call (binary strings, plus "completed agents return cached results") — there is no external API, so buttons must be queued, acknowledged intents gated on `status: idle` from ~/.claude/sessions/<pid>.json, with honest verb definitions. Terminate needs an escalation ladder: SIGTERM was verified to leave an interactive TUI running; SIGHUP/closing the master and SIGKILL work, EOT exits cleanly. A real local PTY-socket surface does exist for background agents (/tmp/cc-daemon-1000/<id>/{control.sock,pty/<id>.sock}, hard-coded 200x50) — documented as deliberately not used, since it is undocumented and version-coupled.

Also: key sessions on (pid, procStart) — procStart equals /proc/<pid>/stat field 22, verified — since sessionId rotates on /clear; the registry keeps ghosts for a passive reader while `claude agents --json` (0.65s, supported, TTY-free) prunes them; expose typed projected endpoints over ~/.claude rather than any path parameter; poll at 250ms (0.39ms per full scan, no stdlib inotify); one process on one port (default 8932, since 8931 is the live monitor); and put app source at repo root as aggregator/, touch-visual/, tests/ with a run_all.sh, keeping .gitignore edits additive so test_shell.py:155 keeps passing.

findings.title: Transport is one-directional by construction: handle() never parses the HTTP method or reads a body, and drain_client() exists only to discard client WS frames — there is no place to put a pause/start/terminate command or a terminal keystroke

Zero auth on a 0.0.0.0 bind: the /ws upgrade validates only sec-websocket-key/version — no Origin, Host, or token check, so any browser tab can read the stream today and would be able to issue control commands tomorrow (CSRF/DNS-rebinding)

The unit of aggregation is a repo-local .claude/local-orchestrators/* folder, not a Claude Code session; ~/.claude/sessions/*.json (sessionId, cwd, status, name, tempo, tmux) — which is exactly Touch's sidebar model — is never read

Visibility is gated on the [monitor] prompt marker inside one wf_*/journal.jsonl, so ordinary session subagents (projects/<slug>/<sessionId>/subagents/agent-*.jsonl + .meta.json — two exist in this session) are entirely invisible

Parallel fan-out is unrepresentable: agent labels are role+attempt only (stage discarded), so the 6 live researchers all render as 'research #1' and monitor.html:287 collapses them into ONE flow-graph node

The event schema is a flat (plan, stage, state) overlay with no node ids, edges or parent/child — it cannot express the n8n-style DAG — and it carries no version field, so no structural change can ever be made to the permanent replayed history

agent_tokens() re-globs and fully re-parses every running agent's entire transcript on every 1s tick (measured 16 ms for 2.26 MB at 6 min in; ~300+ ms/tick extrapolated to a 2-hour 6-agent run) on the same thread that tails the journal

Replay always starts at byte 0 with one WS frame per event, the client clears and rebuilds on every open, the log DOM is never trimmed, and the UI offers a 500 ms full-resync — ~1.5 MB/h of events measured, ≈3 MB/s of replay per tab at 1 h of history

TaskStop/UI stops leave no transcript marker (verified in the CLI binary), so a paused run is indistinguishable from a stalled one and the 60 s quiet debounce will fabricate an 'orchestrator complete done|failed' verdict for it

Restart is Workflow({scriptPath, resumeFromRunId}) cache replay into a NEW journal; load_state() then resets offset=0 and re-emits the whole history into the same events.jsonl, duplicating rows and token deltas — the journal 'key' field that would dedupe it is ignored

All run identity (STATE_DIR, WF_DIR, JOURNAL, WF_NAME, EVENTS, STATE, caps) is module-global and resolved at import, so one process watches exactly one run — the module cannot grow to N sessions without a real refactor
resolve_task_dir() falls back to STATE_DIR for an unknown ?task=, so /ws, /artifacts and /file silently serve a DIFFERENT task's data with 200/101 instead of 404
Catch-all route returns the full monitor.html with 200 for every unknown path and the HTTP method is never parsed — no 404, no 405, no HEAD handling

Multi-writer events.jsonl safety rests on an undocumented, untested 'one write() per record' invariant — verified: 0/800 corrupted with one write() per record, 206/800 corrupted when a record spans two write() calls

Reserved magic names (plan id 'orchestrator'; stages 'plan'/'complete'/'tokens') are string-compared in three files and share the namespace with runtime-generated plan/stage ids, so a colliding id silently hijacks rendering
classify() does up to 3x0.5 s of time.sleep inline in the single poll thread; a 6-way fan-out consumed in one journal chunk can freeze tailing, token ticks and the completion debounce for ~9 s

No test ever starts the server: handle(), stream_events(), drain_client() and main() are untested, and test_frontend.py asserts on monitor.html source text — an approach that does not survive Touch's much larger frontend

Reuse/generalize/replace decision record: reuse verbatim the torn-tail tailer, checkpoint-with-identity, monotonic token deltas, session-rotation path union, safe_artifact_path containment, escape-first rendering, status.sh and the URL-as-state routing

result.summary:
The existing monitoring module is a well-built read-only prototype whose craft should be mined and whose architecture cannot become Touch. Verified correct and worth reusing verbatim: torn-tail tailing with a truncation sentinel (monitor_server.py:330-356, decision_watcher.py:470-491), checkpoint-with-journal-identity plus atomic os.replace (:494-520), monotonic token deltas with message-id dedup (:154-197), /clear-/compact session-rotation path union (:86-100), realpath containment in safe_artifact_path (monitor_server.py:199-212), escape-first markdown + NODE_STATES whitelist discipline (monitor.html:299-321, 463-543), status.sh itself, and the query-string-as-state routing model.

Two blockers stop reuse-in-place. (1) The transport is one-directional by construction: handle() never parses the HTTP method or reads a request body, drain_client() exists purely to discard client frames, and unknown routes return the dashboard with 200 — there is nowhere to put a pause/start/terminate command or a terminal keystroke. (2) There is no authentication, Origin check, or Host check on a 0.0.0.0 bind; harmless for a read-only dashboard, but it makes the control plane CSRF-reachable from any browser tab the moment controls exist. Both must be designed before the first write endpoint.

Nine major scope breaks follow. The aggregation unit is a repo-local task folder, not a Claude Code session (~/.claude/sessions/*.json — sessionId/cwd/status/name/tempo/tmux — is never read, though it is exactly the sidebar model). Visibility is gated on the [monitor] prompt marker in one workflow journal, so ordinary session subagents (two exist in this session, with richer meta: agentType/description/toolUseId/spawnDepth) are invisible. Parallel fan-out is unrepresentable: the watcher builds labels from role+attempt and discards stage, so the six live researchers all read "research #1" and monitor.html:287 collapses them into ONE flow node — the exact case the n8n graph exists to show. The flat (plan, stage, state) schema has no node ids or edges and no version field, so it cannot be the graph source nor evolve over permanent history. agent_tokens() fully re-parses every running agent's whole transcript every second (measured 16 ms/2.26 MB at 6 min; ~300+ ms/tick extrapolated to a 2-hour run) on the thread that also tails the journal. Replay always starts at byte 0, one frame per event, with an untrimmed log DOM and a 500 ms full-resync option — measured ~1.5 MB/h of events, ≈3 MB/s per tab at an hour of history.

Control is where the prior art is structurally blind, and the CLI binary settles it: workflows are background tasks in a task registry, stopped with TaskStop({taskId}) and resumed with Workflow({scriptPath, resumeFromRunId}) — and the binary states stops "leave no transcript marker". So a paused run looks identical to a stalled one and the 60 s quiet debounce will fabricate a completion verdict for it; and a resume replays cached agent() calls into a NEW journal, which load_state() handles by resetting offset=0 and re-emitting the entire history into the same events.jsonl (duplicate rows and token deltas). The journal's per-spawn "key" content hash is the natural idempotency handle and is currently ignored. Finally, one watcher process watches exactly one run with all run identity in module globals, so N sessions x M runs needs a real ~800-line refactor into per-run objects plus a supervisor, not a wrapper.

Minor items: unknown ?task= silently streams a different task instead of 404; no method dispatch or 404 at all; multi-writer append safety rests on an undocumented one-write()-per-record invariant (proved: 0/800 corrupted with one write per record, 206/800 when a record spans two writes — so Touch must not carry terminal output over a shared append file); reserved magic names share the namespace with runtime-generated ids; classify() sleeps in the poll thread (~9 s stall on a 6-way fan-out); and the network layer has zero tests while the frontend is tested by grepping its own source — a posture that must be decided globally now (stdlib socket-level integration tests keep zero-dependency; a JS runner does not).

findings.title: A loop has no OS identity: workflow script runs via vm.runInContext and all its agents live in one claude process (verified: ps shows only PID 622 with 6 concurrent agents), so no per-loop signal/kill target exists

An already-running interactive session has zero external control transport: no listening port, stdin is /dev/pts/0 with dev.tty.legacy_tiocsti=0, no control.sock unless the bg daemon runs, no custom signal handler

Only real control channel is --input-format stream-json control_request; supported subtypes are exactly initialize/interrupt/set_model/set_permission_mode (interrupt verified: killed in-flight background task). No pause or resume verb exists
Claude Code's own workflow pause is abort-plus-checkpoint (kft and tve are the same jxo function): in-flight agent work is destroyed and respawned from scratch on resume
Restart exists only as Workflow({scriptPath,resumeFromRunId}), is same-session only, and is a model-facing tool call — an external page can only request it, never perform it
journal.jsonl is both the resume cache and the watcher's byte-offset tail source; editing/truncating it to force a stage re-run silently freezes decision_watcher.py forever
No harness-level rollback: aborting an implementer leaves half-written source files, and the next attempt resumes onto that dirty tree, burning attempts out of MAX_ATTEMPTS

PreToolUse HTTP hooks are a working external control plane (verified: held a Bash call 20s then allowed); payload carries session_id, transcript_path, cwd, permission_mode, agent_id, agent_type, tool_name, tool_input

Hook-based pause is bounded: it lands only at tool boundaries (unbounded latency during inference), expires at the 600000ms hook timeout, and deny is surfaced to the model as a tool error that pollutes the loop
Hooks are session-scoped config with no verified live reload for an already-running process; Touch must launch sessions with a static --settings hook file rather than writing settings post hoc

SIGSTOP freezes the whole session (verified: survived a 70s stop) but hits every loop at once, does not stop already-spawned child processes, risks API/proxy stream reaping, and makes the session unable to receive interrupt
Start is fully achievable via three routes (stream-json child, Touch-hosted PTY, claude --bg); no single process gives both structured control and terminal fidelity, so Touch needs both
Terminate has two meanings: interrupt (session survives, verified) vs process kill (all loops die, workflows/<runId>.json completion record never written, orchestrator badge stuck running)
Private bg-session IPC (/tmp/cc-daemon-<uid>/<hash8>/control.sock, pty/<id>.sock, pipe.key auth, {t:kill|resize|ping} frames) is an undocumented protocol that must not carry Touch's headline feature
Per-agent kill/pause/skip/retry already exist in-process (ISd/Vfr/zfr with user-skip/user-retry AbortError) but are wired only to the Ink TUI panel — no socket, flag or control_request reaches them
TaskStop and Workflow are model-facing tools, so any Touch verb built on them is advisory; workflows can also be disabled outright by policy, requiring the loop controls to degrade

Five things are semantically impossible (suspend/resume of inference, process-level per-loop pause, cross-session workflow resume, controlling a foreign session, undoing an aborted agent's edits) and must be scoped out explicitly

result.summary: A "loop" is a JS program running via vm.runInContext inside ONE claude process — verified by ps (PID 622 only) while six workflow agents ran concurrently — so no loop, agent or attempt has an OS identity to signal. For an already-running interactive session there is NO external control transport at all: claude listens on no TCP port, stdin is /dev/pts/0 with dev.tty.legacy_tiocsti=0 (injection disabled), no control.sock exists without the bg daemon, and no custom signal handler exists beyond terminate. The only supported channel is --input-format stream-json, whose control_request parser accepts exactly initialize/interrupt/set_model/set_permission_mode — verified live (interrupt returned success and killed the in-flight background task). Of the README's four verbs: START is fully achievable (three routes; structured control and terminal fidelity cannot come from one process). TERMINATE is achievable, cleanly via interrupt, destructively via process kill (which also loses the workflows/<runId>.json completion record, written only at run end). RESTART exists only as Workflow({scriptPath, resumeFromRunId}) — same-session only, a model-facing tool call, resumable only at agent() boundaries, with in-flight agents respawned from scratch and no working-tree rollback. PAUSE as specified does not exist: the harness's own "pause" (kft) is the same function as kill (tve) with a different status string. The one genuinely new finding is that hooks are a working external control plane — a PreToolUse HTTP hook verifiably held a tool call 20s then released it, and its payload carries agent_id/agent_type, so Touch can pause, step and gate a single agent while siblings run; the limits are tool-boundary latency, a 600000ms timeout ceiling, and deny being visible to the model. Notably, per-agent kill/pause/skip/retry already exist in-process (ISd/Vfr/zfr) but are wired only to the Ink TUI with no transport out. 17 findings written to the findings file, including a five-item list of what is semantically impossible.

findings.title: No live channel into an already-running interactive session; Touch must own the process it displays
"Pause" does not exist in any Claude Code channel; only interrupt/kill/restart-with-cache do
A real PTY multiplexer (--bg-pty-host, framed unix socket, scrollback replay) is directly invocable and should back the terminal page
PTY socket streams output to any connector unauthenticated; only writes are token-gated (DATA gate fails open)
PTY channel is a private, version-coupled interface; needs a capability probe and a declared fallback
SDK stream-json is the supported live channel and carries a real control_request protocol (interrupt, stop_task, set_permission_mode, can_use_tool)
31 hook events enumerated with payloads; the only push channel for sessions Touch did not spawn
Hooks are strictly blocking (measured 3.10s added to a 67ms tool) with a 600s default timeout
MessageDisplay streams text deltas but runs forceSyncExecution on the render path; unusable as a transport
Live subagent attribution solved by SubagentStart/Stop + agent_id on nested tool events (70ms spawn latency); spawn tool_name is Agent, not Task
Transcript tailing is message-granular with 1-5s bursts; cannot back a terminal view
Session registry has no heartbeat (status=busy, updatedAt 854s stale); liveness must come from /proc + procStart
Subagent content is not in the parent transcript and workflow agents carry no role on disk; the [monitor] prompt marker is load-bearing
Background agents already expose loop state, timeline, PTY socket and auth token that Touch can read for free
Live channels are unix sockets/local files behind the sandbox boundary; bind 0.0.0.0, avoid port 8931 collision, expose /health
Remote Control is an api.anthropic.com cloud relay with attestation; reject it as a transport
Hook observability (hook_started/hook_response) exists only in stream-json mode; PTY mode reports nothing
Same event arrives on up to three channels at different times; event schema has no id for dedup
Killed runs leave journal 'started' with no 'result' forever; stale must be a distinct UI state
CLAUDE_PTY_RECORD writes a private binary format; tee the frames Touch already receives instead

result.summary: 20 findings on Touch's live path, all verified empirically against CLI 2.1.220, the running session (pid 622), and throwaway experiments in /tmp/claude-1000/liveio. Two blockers. (1) LIVEIO-1: there is NO way to attach to an already-running interactive Claude session — /proc/622/fd shows only /dev/pts/0, no unix socket exists until a background session is started, and daemon roster.json lists only daemon workers. Touch must OWN (spawn) every session it displays; README.md's "web view over claude code session" cannot mean mirroring the user's existing terminal. (2) LIVEIO-9: "pause" (README.md:6) does not exist anywhere in the CLI's control vocabulary — only interrupt, kill, stop_task and hook deny/block. Honest implementations are a blocking gate hook at SubagentStart/PreToolUse, or a cooperative control-file check inside the workflow script; both pause only at an agent boundary, which the UI must say. Restart is real and cheap: the Workflow runtime memoises agent() calls by prompt hash (journal key "v2:<sha256>"), so re-running with the same runId replays completed agents ("100% cache hit"). The big positive: I proved, twice, that a raw ANSI terminal stream with input, resize and kill is available locally — `<versioned-binary> --bg-pty-host <sock> <cols> <rows> -- <cmd> [args]` opens a unix socket with a 5-byte-header frame protocol (uint32BE len + uint8 kind; kind 0 = PTY bytes, kind 1 = JSON control), replays a 256KB scrollback ring then sends {"t":"live"}, and fans out to multiple subscribers. I drove a real interactive Claude REPL through it (36 frames, first at t+0.00s). Caveats: output is streamed to any connector unauthenticated (LIVEIO-3, and the input gate fails open when the tokens file is unreadable), and the interface is private/version-coupled (LIVEIO-4), so it needs a capability probe plus SDK stream-json as the declared fallback. For the graph page, hooks are decisive: all 31 hook events enumerated from the binary, every payload carries agent_id/agent_type, SubagentStart fires 70ms after spawn and SubagentStop hands over agent_transcript_path — but hooks are strictly blocking (measured: a sleep-3 PreToolUse hook added 3.10s to a 67ms tool; default timeout is 600s), so the hook must only append a line to a file. Transcript tailing is message-granular with 1-5s bursts and cannot back a terminal. The session registry has no heartbeat (622.json said status=busy with updatedAt 854s stale), so liveness must come from /proc+procStart or `claude agents --json`. Remote Control is an api.anthropic.com cloud relay and should be rejected.

findings.title: usage is duplicated on every split assistant record; naive summing over-counts tokens 2.09x (115605 vs 55396) - dedupe by message.id
thinking text is never persisted: all 44/44 thinking blocks have thinking:"", only signature survives
transcript is not append-only: performRemoveByUuid truncates and performCompactTranscript whole-file-rewrites; byte-offset tailing breaks
mode/permission-mode/ai-title/last-prompt are last-wins state re-appended every 32KiB, not events (20/20/15/19 copies in 297 lines)
writes batch on a 100ms timer into one appendFile up to 100MB: torn tails guaranteed (max line 46567 bytes); measured flush latency +0.10s
/clear starts a NEW sessionId and new file under the same pid; transcript file is created lazily (probe had lastSessionId but no .jsonl)
sessions/<pid>.json is not a heartbeat (863s stale while busy) and is written non-atomically; use /proc/<pid> + procStart for liveness
no session-end record in the transcript; a crashed session is indistinguishable from an idle one
async Workflow runs have no completion record in the parent transcript (status: async_launched only); must watch journal.jsonl
workflow journal entries carry no timestamps and result is a Python-repr string, not JSON
workflow subagent meta.json omits description/toolUseId; only the [monitor] prompt marker identifies plan/stage/role
faithful terminal replay is not reconstructible; built-in asciicast recorder exists but CLAUDE_CODE_TERMINAL_RECORDING produced no .cast in 3 probes
retention sweep deletes the transcript AND rm -rf's the whole <sessionId>/ subagent+workflow tree
exactly one content block per record; UI must group turns by (requestId, message.id) or a turn renders as 3 bubbles
transcripts and history.jsonl hold unredacted file contents, command output and every prompt; a 0.0.0.0-bound unauthenticated server exfiltrates them
progress records (bash_progress, tool_heartbeat, agent_progress) are in the schema but zero appear on disk across all sessions
hooks (SessionEnd reason, PermissionRequest, SubagentStart/Stop, PreCompact) carry data absent from the transcript; make hook install a design decision
~/.claude.json lastSessionId points at an exited session and lastCost/lastTotal*Tokens are 0; never read cost or current session from it, never write to it
file-history backups give real pre-edit contents but are keyed by sessionId and die with it; prefer toolUseResult.structuredPatch
prompt queue is visible via queue-operation + attachment/queued_command but is last-wins, so only the live tail is trustworthy

result.summary:
Researched the persisted session data model from real files under ~/.claude plus targeted `grep -a`/`dd` reads of the 275MB CLI binary (v2.1.220), and empirical probes in /tmp. 20 findings, 3 blockers.

WHAT EXISTS. The session JSONL is a mix of four record classes, and the CLI's own classification table (binary byte 259354279) is the ground truth: `transcript` (user/assistant/system/attachment), `boundary-cleared` (progress, file-history-*, last-prompt), `accumulate` (content-replacement, fork-context-ref, frame-link) and `last-wins` (mode, permission-mode, ai-title, custom-title, summary, tag, queue-operation, worktree-state, pr-link, bridge-session, …). Siblings: `<sid>/subagents/agent-<id>.jsonl` + `.meta.json`, `<sid>/subagents/workflows/<runId>/journal.jsonl`, `~/.claude/sessions/<pid>.json`, `~/.claude/file-history/<sid>/<hash>@vN`, `~/.claude/history.jsonl`, `~/.claude.json`. There is no `projects/<sid>/workflows/<runId>.json` — that path in the brief does not exist on disk.

THREE BLOCKERS.
1. `usage` is copied onto every split assistant record of one API response — 50 of 63 response groups span multiple records, so summing per record over-counts output tokens 2.09x (115,605 vs 55,396 deduped by `message.id`). `.claude/shared/monitoring/decision_watcher.py:154` already dedupes correctly; reuse it.
2. Thinking text is never persisted: all 44/44 thinking blocks in the main transcript, and every one in all 8 subagent transcripts, have `thinking: ""` with only a signature — despite `alwaysThinkingEnabled: true`. A transcript-sourced "thinking" pane is永 empty.
3. The transcript is not append-only. `performRemoveByUuid` truncates and rewrites the tail (the file shrinks); `performCompactTranscript` rewrites the whole file via `<file>.compact.tmp.<hex>` + rename, dropping everything before the compact boundary. Byte-offset tailing silently freezes.

LATENCY (measured, good news). The writer batches on a `FLUSH_INTERVAL_MS = 100` timer; a poll started inside a Bash call saw that call's own `tool_use` record land +0.10s later, before the tool finished. Intra-turn visibility is real and sub-second with zero instrumentation. The cost is torn tails: batches are one `appendFile` up to 100 MiB, and observed lines reach 46 KB — cut at the last `\n` and defer the remainder.

LIFECYCLE. `/clear` starts a NEW sessionId and new file under the same pid (CLI's own command description), so the sidebar must key on pid and re-resolve sessionId every poll. The transcript file is created lazily — a probe session produced `lastSessionId` in `~/.claude.json` but no `.jsonl` at all. There is no session-end record (a cleanly `/exit`-ed session just stops after `Goodbye!`). `sessions/<pid>.json` is not a heartbeat: it was 863s stale while the session was busy running six subagents, and is written with a non-atomic read-modify-writeFile. Liveness must be `/proc/<pid>` + `procStart` (verified = `/proc/pid/stat` field 22).

AGENT GRAPH. Async `Workflow` runs return only `status: "async_launched"` and never get a completion record in the parent transcript — the run graph exists solely in `journal.jsonl` (which has `started`/`result` entries with **no timestamps**, and a `result` that is a Python-repr string, not JSON). Workflow subagent `.meta.json` is a 63-byte stub with no description or toolUseId, so per-node labels can only come from the `[monitor] plan=… stage=… role=… attempt=…` marker in the agent's first user record.

TERMINAL VIEW VERDICT. Reconstructible: prompts (incl. slash/bash-mode forms), assistant text, every tool call with full input, every tool result with full untruncated output (richer than the TTY, which truncates), turn durations, usage, model/effort/skill attribution, the whole subagent tree, file diffs. Not reconstructible: reasoning, streaming deltas, ANSI, permission dialogs, status line, system prompt, intra-tool progress (`progress` records are in the schema but literally zero exist on disk), and session end. The binary contains a complete asciicast v2 recorder writing `<sid>-<ts>.cast`, but `CLAUDE_CODE_TERMINAL_RECORDING` produced no file in three probes (`-p` with `1`, `-p` with a path, and a real pty) and the literal appears only in env-schema tables — do not plan around it. The plan must explicitly choose: semantic re-render of the transcript, or Touch owns the PTY.

TWO CROSS-CUTTING RISKS. The CLI's retention sweep unlinks the transcript and `rm -rf`s the entire `<sessionId>/` subagent tree, so Touch must own its history rather than reading `~/.claude` as an archive. And transcripts plus `history.jsonl` hold unredacted file contents, command output and every prompt ever typed — with a 0.0.0.0 bind and a published port mandated by the sandbox, every transcript route needs a token.

Merged 6 research reports (110 findings) plus driver context into one plan: 6 conflict resolutions decided against primary sources (driver overridden on write latency and bg-pty-host invocability; confirmed on tool-results spill via binary re-grep), 14 binding global decisions (Touch hosts sessions rather than attaching; owned vs observed class split drives every affordance; touch-events-v2 single stream with ref-union keys in repo-local .touch/; (pid,procStart)/uuid/message.id/(runId,key,ordinal) identity; Python 3.11 stdlib asyncio one process on 8932 with vendored xterm.js and hand-rolled SVG graph; per-boot token + Origin allowlist + typed endpoints; honest control table — start/terminate deterministic v1, stop/restart model-mediated with observed confirmation, pause only as hook-gate at tool boundaries v1.5, suspend impossible), and 23 ordered implementation items each with files, resolved finding ids, approach, and test coverage, plus discarded-findings register and 10 UNVERIFIED items with cheapest settling experiments.
